label: PF Backlog 597
title: EDP-16: Object lifecycle (versioning/lock/retention), signed-URL policy, delete/replica/backup reconciliation
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

decisions.note: Gate 1 approved by HIL: action all 16 Gate 1.5 findings; COMPLIANCE irreversible documented; S3 lock verified via header-stub tests.

brief.problem: Objects have no lifecycle/retention/lock guarantees and ad-hoc URLs bypass policy
brief.why: Enterprise compliance and safe delete/backup semantics

objective: Define and enforce object lifecycle rules (versioning, object lock/retention), a central signed-URL policy with TTL bounds, and a read-only reconciliation scanner that reports drift between a manifest and the object store.
acceptance_criteria: ObjectStore exposes an optional LifecycleCapable capability: ApplyLifecycle(policy) and ObjectLifecycle(key) (retention mode/until, legal hold, versioning) with a typed ErrUnsupported for providers that cannot honour it; S3 implements object-lock retention (GOVERNANCE/COMPLIANCE) and legal hold, local returns ErrUnsupported.

PutOptions.Retention/Immutable are enforced or explicitly rejected per provider: S3 applies object-lock headers (and fails when the bucket lacks object-lock), local documents that it cannot lock and fails closed when Immutable+TTL is requested without support.

Central signed-URL policy (go/objpolicy): Mint validates method allowlist (GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE), TTL bounds (min 30s, max 15m, default 5m), key prefix/tenant guard, and provider SignedURL capability; it never mints for providers without SignedURLs and returns typed errors.

Reconciliation scanner (go/objreconcile): compares a manifest (key, size, checksum) against ObjectStore.List/Head, reports missing, orphaned, size-mismatch and checksum-mismatch entries with counts and a deterministic JSON report; read-only (no deletes).

Tests: lifecycle capability conformance for local (unsupported) and S3 (skipped without endpoint); signed-URL policy unit tests (TTL bounds, method allowlist, unsupported provider); reconciliation unit tests with a fake store (missing/orphan/size/checksum).
Verification: go build/test for the affected modules, lint clean, precheck PASS; no HTTP/API surface change (needs_api=false).
in_scope: LifecycleCapable interface + S3 object-lock/retention + local fail-closed unsupported.
go/objpolicy signed-URL minting (method allowlist, TTL bounds, provider capability).
go/objreconcile manifest-vs-store drift scanner + JSON report.
Conformance/unit tests for local and S3 paths.
approach: Interface-first: add LifecycleCapable as an optional interface (no break to ObjectStore), implement object-lock/retention in s3store, add a small policy package for signed URLs, and a reconciliation package with a CLI-free library API; tests use the local adapter and a fake store, with S3 tests gated on PF_S3_ENDPOINT.
risks: Object-lock semantics differ by provider; unsupported combinations must fail closed.
Signed-URL TTL policy is a security boundary: defaults must be conservative and tested.
Reconciliation must never delete; a false orphan report is advisory only.
rollback: Feature-flag lifecycle enforcement; providers without capability degrade to no-op with warning.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the provider-neutral ObjectStore interface (BI-PF-1299) and S3 adapter (BI-PF-1306) with lifecycle capabilities: versioning, object-lock/legal-hold, retention rules, signed-URL policy; reconcile deletes/replicas/backups via residency manifest from BI-PF-1304.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1306 S3 adapter at done
REQUIRES BI-PF-1304 residency manifest at done
conflict_findings: Low: S3 adapter (BI-PF-1306) files may still be warm; coordinate interface changes
duplication_findings: core/lock_manager.py is an in-process lock, not bucket object-lock — pattern reuse only, no duplication
No existing object lifecycle/signed-URL code in candidates; core/*_policy.py files are governance policies (different domain)
analysis.rationale: Builds directly on existing storage interfaces/adapter; adds capability layer rather than new component. Reuse-first honored.
assumptions: Lifecycle features are optional capabilities on ObjectStore interface
Signed URLs are minted centrally, never stored
Manifest from BI-PF-1304 is authoritative for allowed regions
risks: Provider capability gaps (local filesystem, non-S3) for object-lock/versioning
Retention rules conflicting with residency/backup retention
missing_info: Default retention periods per data class
Whether object-lock applies in dev/local mode
Signed-URL TTL ceiling and audience model

context_review.reason: Interfaces, adapter, and manifest exist or are pinned; only policy values need human input.
